speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms, can you tell me exactly when the weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm started?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of anabolic steroid use and significant weight loss, I need to rule out malignancy or structural lesions. Have you noticed any lumps, pain in your neck or shoulder, or changes in your skin or eyes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain or numbness radiate from your neck down your arm, and do you have any weakness or sensory changes in your legs? I also need to check if you have any difficulty with bowel or bladder control.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diabetes Social history: Drinks 2-7 alcoholic beverages per day. Has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since he was 25. Uses anabolic steroids.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the progressive weakness, sensory loss, and significant weight loss, I need to rule out a spinal cord compression or peripheral nerve lesion. REQUEST TEST: MRI_of_the_Spine_and_Brachial_Plexus

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRI is normal, I need to evaluate your peripheral nerves directly. Do you have any sensory loss in a "glove" distribution, and is there any muscle wasting or fasciculations in your right arm?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent fevers, changes in vision, difficulty speaking, or changes in balance.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the significant weight loss and heavy smoking history, we must rule out a paraneoplastic syndrome or Pancoast tumor, so REQUEST TEST: Chest_CTA. Additionally, REQUEST TEST: EMG_NCS_right_arm to evaluate for peripheral nerve damage.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal imaging and EMG rule out structural and peripheral nerve causes, pointing towards a metabolic or toxic etiology given your history of heavy alcohol use and diabetes. Do you experience tingling or burning sensations in your feet as well, and have you noticed any difficulty with coordination or balance?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent fevers, changes in vision, difficulty speaking, or changes in balance.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of diabetes, alcohol use, and steroid use, I suspect a toxic-metabolic neuropathy or diabetic amyotrophy. REQUEST TEST: HbA1c and Vitamin_B12_level

speaker: Doctor
text: With metabolic and structural causes ruled out, the significant weight loss and smoking history strongly suggest a paraneoplastic syndrome or an occult malignancy. REQUEST TEST: CT_of_the_Abdomen_and_Pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative workup for structural, metabolic, and common paraneoplastic causes, I suspect an autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder exacerbated by steroid withdrawal or an atypical presentation of a paraneoplastic syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Lambert-Eaton Myasthenic Syndrome
